Right image: PySchool 2025's website The new versio of the website has a "escape room setup", where each room is a challenge to be solved, focused on one key aspect of Python (strings, floats, lists, dicts, etc). Brief explanations of each concept are provided, when needed.
Left image: PySchool 2024's website The previous version of the website allowed to validate the tech stack: using quarto+pyodide was simple to develop and easy to use by students.

PySchool 2024's class: We tested 2 room setups and learned that a more relaxed and interactive class lead to better learning and was preferred by students. Highschoolers liked the event (average evaluation of 9.3/10) but suggested some improvements over the content and delivery.
Traditional lab setup does not allow for easy interaction!
Traditional classes are boring!
Challenges and discussion keeps students engaged.

Setup quarto+pyodide allowed us to code a simple website in Spanish (pyschool.cl) that does not requires users to install Python! It's simpler to use than jupyter notebooks. It does not require an account and students can use the website any time, after PySchool.
PySchool 2024 Intro to Python (1h) and Intro to Data Analysis (1h). ≈100 students & 3 dates in Valparaíso, Chile.

FUTURE

MOTIVATION Events organized by Python Chile (PyDay and PyCon) were aimed towards grownups. We dreamed of an event targetting highschool students. We can't teach Python in a day, but we can show how simple and fun coding in Python can be, and motivate students to start learning Python!

tspan.tspan: TLDR; We motivated highschoolers to learn Python, using a simple website powered by quarto+pyodide. They loved it!
